page: Amazon Web Services r8gb.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and ARMv9 architecture. The system provides 32 dedicated physical cores using AWS Neoverse-V2 processors running at 2.8 GHz, with one thread per core and no simultaneous multithreading. It includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 36 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 256.0 GB, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance carries no onboard local NVMe storage and includes no GPU accelerators, while network bandwidth provides a 67 Gbps baseline.

Benchmark results show significant capability in memory subsystems and multi-threaded throughput. Large-block memory bandwidth tests place the instance in the top 10 percent of evaluated hardware, reaching 427.21 GB/sec for uncached read-only blocks and 200.77 GB/sec for write operations. PassMark database testing yields 47,851.85 operations alongside a top-tier multi-core Geekbench score of 21,725.0. Redis SET operations hit 67.66 million operations per second, supported by 74.31 GB/sec in static web throughput. Single-core results across stress-ng and Geekbench register within the middle 50 percent, reflecting standard single-thread clock targets rather than compute-focused peak frequency.

The absence of local disks necessitates reliance on external network-attached volumes, making network throughput a critical operational factor. The architecture achieves strong resource efficiency for memory-intensive processes by dedicating full physical cores to each vCPU, eliminating thread contention. Workload fit includes in-memory key-value databases, Redis clusters, large-scale caching engines, distributed memory-based data transformation pipelines, and high-concurrency compilation tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services r8gb.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores at 2.8 GHz, 256.0 GB of system memory, and a 67 Gbps baseline network connection managed by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Configured with a dedicated core-per-vCPU design, the system exhibits top-tier memory bandwidth, reaching 427.21 GB/sec in large uncached reads and 200.77 GB/sec in uncached writes, accompanied by strong Redis and database processing results. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware accelerators, requiring external network-attached storage architectures. Given its 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, consistent multi-core performance, and high memory throughput, r8gb.8xlarge is primarily suited for in-memory caching platforms, distributed relational or non-relational database services, and large-footprint analytical workloads.
